I wish wearing flatirons.simple: I wish that wearing heavy irons on our heads would stop us from growing up.

for ridicule is often.grammar: This is a short wise saying. It compares two things with 'harder ... than'. The word 'for' gives the reason why the young man hesitated.

It takes people a long time.simple: People need a long time to learn the difference between talent and genius.

straws show which way.simple: Small signs show which way things are going, and I have found out several things today.
straws show which way.grammar: 'Straws show which way the wind blows' is a saying: small signs tell you what is going to happen. 'Which way the wind blows' is a noun clause, the object of 'show'.

I don't know whether the shearing.simple: I do not know if the cutting of her hair made our wild girl more serious.

In order that we may start afresh.grammar: 'In order that we may...' shows purpose. 'May' is a formal word here, like 'so that we can'. 'It will be well to begin' means 'it is good to begin'.

he turned and strained his eyes.simple: He turned and strained his eyes to see the island. A greater taker of power than even Napoleon now made the island interesting to him.
he turned and strained his eyes.grammar: 'Which a greater usurper than even Napoleon now made interesting' is a clause that tells more about 'island'. A usurper is a person who takes power that is not his. Here it is a joke: the 'usurper' seems to be Laurie's feeling for Jo. 'Greater ... than even Napoleon' is a comparison.

if John goes on so much longer.grammar: 'If John goes on ... I might as well be' mixes a real 'if' with 'might as well', which says that one thing is no different from the other. 'Widowed' means that a husband has died.

as if he felt that justice.simple: It was as if Demi felt that being fair can be softened by being kind.
as if he felt that justice.grammar: 'As if' introduces something that only seems true. 'Tempered with' means 'made softer by'. The verb phrase is in the passive: 'justice was tempered'.

It takes two flints.simple: You need two flints to make a fire. You are as cool and soft as snow.
It takes two flints.grammar: The first part says 'It takes + noun + to + verb'. The second part uses 'as ... as' to compare Amy to snow, which cannot make fire.

So well that I wish we might.simple: We row so well together that I wish we could always share one boat.
So well that I wish we might.grammar: 'Pull in the same boat' is a pun: it means rowing in one boat and also living one life together. 'I wish we might' uses 'might' for something that one hopes for but cannot be sure of.

Not being a dog in the manger.simple: I am not selfish like a dog in the manger. I am the happiest man alive, and I promise you I can dance at Jo's wedding with a heart as light as my heels.

he would have been glad of his handkerch.simple: The Professor found it so touching that he would have liked to have his handkerchief, if he could have reached it.

So she took Amy in hand.grammar: 'Take in hand' is a phrase meaning 'take charge of'. 'As she herself had been taught' is a past passive clause that compares how she taught Amy with how she had been taught.

it takes much folly.grammar: 'It takes + noun + to + verb' is a pattern for what is needed to do something. Here 'It' stands for the whole idea, and 'much folly, sin, or misery' is the thing needed.
